title: Positive odd-Matsubara resolvent expansion of the capped Gibbs kernel
question: Can the exact theta-half hyperbolic-tangent Gibbs kernel be decomposed into positive odd-Matsubara resolvent layers so that future locality estimates can be proved layer by layer without a uniform spectral gap?
method: Use the positive partial-fraction expansion tanh(x)=sum_n 8*x/((2*n+1)^2*pi^2+4*x^2) with x=beta*Delta/2, and define the corresponding absolute-Liouvillian resolvent layer.
Check positivity and monotone partial sums, compare the direct tanh kernel with a finite N-term sum, and apply the explicit odd-square tail envelope.
Evaluate the exact and partial-kernel shells on every R-373 actual-Q3 history context, retaining both orientations, signs, adjoints, beta values and all prefixes.
Reconstruct the same calculation independently and compile Lean R374 for symbolic odd-frequency positivity and finite-sum monotonicity.
finding: The positive odd-Matsubara partial sums stay below the exact hyperbolic-tangent kernel within the declared numerical tolerance, and the resulting shell remainder is bounded by the computed positive tail form on every R-373 context. The decomposition supplies a resolvent-layer interface, but it does not itself prove a cutoff-, volume- or source-uniform locality bound.
decision_reason: R-374 changes the analytic order of attack: instead of seeking one global capped estimate, prove a positive locality estimate for each Matsubara resolvent layer and sum a controlled tail. This retains transition-energy information and avoids assuming a uniform spectral gap. The finite layer checks do not close resolvent locality or common alpha, so no promotion is justified.

adversarial_review.check: The infinite partial-fraction formula is treated as an analytic interface; executable assertions concern finite partial sums and direct tanh comparisons only.
Partial sums are checked not to exceed the direct kernel, while the one-sided tail envelope is checked independently.
Delta=0 has a zero numerator and no transition-energy division.
Every denominator contains a positive odd frequency square and a nonnegative beta-squared transition term.
All R-373 prefix positions, split orders, signs and adjoints are retained.
The decomposition does not erase the finite edge growth; no uniform conclusion is inferred.
The doubled-bond Gibbs weights remain a local finite proxy rather than a global interacting KMS state.
Lean proves symbolic layer positivity and finite monotonicity, not the infinite series, spectra, traces or limits.
Resolvent locality, common core, common alpha, OS/KMS/GNS dynamics, gap, continuum, C6, Sector-A and Pre-A remain open.

next_action: Prove a source-, volume- and cutoff-uniform locality estimate for each positive odd-Matsubara resolvent layer on a Hamiltonian-derived common core, then sum the layers with a controlled tail.
boundary: T0 claim-nonbearing finite odd-Matsubara resolvent-layer checkpoint only. The proposed scalar series interface and finite partial sums do not establish resolvent locality, common core, common alpha, OS/KMS/GNS dynamics, gap, continuum, C6, Sector-A or Pre-A.
no_overclaim: R-374 changes the analytic interface but does not prove a uniform Q3 estimate or any QFT closure.
